column1: # loop_bounded.tsv -- TH8K-009 reviewed loop dispositions (the BOUNDED/SAFE set).
# file<TAB>function<TAB>reason.  Command-surface functions whose loop(s) do NOT
# poll Th8_Ready because the iteration count is bounded, not because the loop
# was overlooked.  discover_loops.tcl treats a function here (or in
# poll_required.tsv) as accounted for.  Four bound classes are used:
#   CONST  -- loop over a fixed/compile-time structure (e.g. a static command
#             table); bound is a small constant.
#   ARGV   -- loop over THIS command's argument vector (argc); every arg was a
#             word the (now-polled) parser produced in this same invocation, so
#             the loop is <=2x the parse it is already bounded by.
#   HASHENUM-- enumerate an interp command/variable/package table; each entry was
#             created by a step-counted command, so <=2x amplification.
#   SPLIT  -- loop over the ELEMENTS of a list/dict value, materialized by
#             Th8_SplitList; per-element work is a pointer/length copy, and the
#             element count is bounded by the (step-limited) work that built the
#             value.  Polling these is a candidate future hardening; unlike the
#             string value-loops (per-char classification/rewrite, which DO poll)
#             the per-element cost here is trivial.
#   CAPPED -- loop bounded by an explicit constant cap.
#   BODY   -- per-iteration Th8_Eval of a script body re-enters the polled
#   PARSE  -- the parser scanning attacker-supplied input.  A LINEAR pass whose
#             length is bounded by the size of the input/value being parsed --
#             which is itself bounded by the script size or by the
#             allocation-quota- and step-limited work that built the value -- so
#             it is not an amplification.  The parser (th8NextWord) is also
#             shared with the debug suspend/resume path, where a cancel poll
#             would treat TH8_SUSPEND as a fatal error and abort a resumed
#             script; and it runs on every word during evaluation, where a poll
#             inflates the step counter for short words.  Cancellation of the
#             surrounding work is the eval loop's job (it polls per command).
